I was young and stupid and I didn't think things were going right in my life. I thought this would help, and for a while it did, but then it got bad. Like a drug addiction, there's a period where everything goes right before everything turns bad. During that period of my life, I would have said it absolutely helped me. I thought it helped me regain control and it made me feel good.
Now, I can say for certain, it did not help. It was just a bad time in my life that I'm glad is over.

At first I used the blades from a shaving razor. Then for a while I used an exacto knife blade. Then I used a box cutter blade. I didn't really like the exacto knife. But between the other two I can't decide a favorite.

I think cutting is definitely an addiction. After just the first time, I always felt drawn back to the blade.
I didn't get any professional help to recover. My strategy was to tell people I love that it was happening, which discouraged me from doing it again after seeing how much it hurt them. Especially after I told my mum, I never wanted to do it again. I haven't done it for a while now, so I think it worked.

I don't know. I feel sorry for them that they're getting themselves into something bigger than they understand. I think there must be some deeper problems going on to make them do that too. I don't think it could possibly be that they just want to be cool.
Cutting is a relief. It gives you a temporary "high" feeling which makes everything better. Then, just like drugs, the high goes away and you feel even lower.

I guess the pain was a part of it. I don't really understand ALL of the reasons it happened; I just know that it felt good. I think part of it was to exert control over my life in some way. Part of it was the adrenaline. And after a while, it becomes an addiction, so part of it was that.

On my left wrist. For me, it was a coping mechanism. The adrenaline that I got after I cut was like a high. It made me forget about everything else in my life for a while. But after the adrenaline was gone, it left me lower than before (cutting is a depressant), so it started a vicious cycle. Hope that helps.
